source_text: Σολομὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ῥοβοάμ, Ῥοβοὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιά, Ἀβιὰ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν ⸂Ἀσάφ,
english_snapshot: Solomon fathered Rehoboam[a], Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Asa,' matching the king of Judah named in 1 Kings 15 and 2 Chronicles 14–16; the Greek text here reads 'Asaph.'

source_text: Ἀσὰφ⸃ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσαφάτ, Ἰωσαφὰτ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωράμ, Ἰωρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ὀζίαν,
english_snapshot: Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat[a], Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Asa' instead of 'Asaph'; 'Asa' also matches the Judean king named in the Old Testament genealogy.

source_text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάλιν γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.
english_snapshot: Jesus said to him[a][b], “Again it is written: ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

signals.text: This cites Deuteronomy 6:16. The Greek “the Lord” reflects the Septuagint’s rendering of the divine name.

source_text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ ⸀αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
english_snapshot: But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to the judgment[a]; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be liable to the council; and whoever says[b][c][d][e], ‘Fool,’ will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

signals.text: Some manuscripts add 'without cause' after 'is angry with his brother.' The earliest and best-attested reading omits it.

source_text: Προσέχετε ⸀δὲ τὴν ⸀δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
english_snapshot: But be careful not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them[a]; otherwise[b], you have no reward from your Father in the heavens.

signals.text: Or 'your acts of righteousness.' A textual variant reads 'your almsgiving.'

source_text: Καὶ ⸂ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ⸃ εἰς τὸ πέραν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν ⸀Γαδαρηνῶν ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ δύο δαιμονιζόμενοι ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἐξερχόμενοι, χαλεποὶ λίαν ὥστε μὴ ἰσχύειν τινὰ παρελθεῖν διὰ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἐκείνης.
english_snapshot: And when he came to the other side[a], into the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men met him, coming out of the tombs[b], so extremely fierce that no one was able to pass along that road.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “Gergesenes” or “Gerasenes” instead of “Gadarenes.”

source_text: Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ ⸀Θαδδαῖος,
english_snapshot: Philip and Bartholomew[a], Thomas and Matthew the tax collector, James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus,

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “Lebbaeus” (or “Lebbaeus called Thaddaeus”), and Luke’s apostolic lists name “Judas son of James” in the corresponding place.

source_text: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·
english_snapshot: Jesus sent out these twelve, instructing them, saying, “Do not go on any road to the Gentiles[a], and do not enter a town of the Samaritans[b].”

signals.text: Or “a Samaritan town.”

source_text: ἦλθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, τελωνῶν φίλος καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν. καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ τῶν ⸀ἔργων αὐτῆς.
english_snapshot: The Son of Man came eating and drinking[a], and they say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard[b], a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ And wisdom was justified by her works.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'children' instead of 'works': 'wisdom was justified by her children.'

source_text: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ⸂ἔφαγον, ὃ⸃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις;
english_snapshot: how he entered into the house of God and ate the bread of the Presence[a], which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him[b], but only for the priests?

signals.text: Some manuscripts/readings have 'he ate' instead of 'they ate.'

source_text: ⸂εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ἑστήκασιν, ζητοῦντές σοι λαλῆσαι.⸃
english_snapshot: Then someone said to him[a], “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to you.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit this verse.

source_text: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ ⸀καταβολῆς.
english_snapshot: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled[a], saying: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “from the foundation of the world.”

source_text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός; ⸀οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ ⸀Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;
english_snapshot: Is this not the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary[a][b], and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Joses' instead of 'Joseph.'

source_text: ⸀οὐ μὴ ⸀τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα ⸀αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε ⸂τὸν λόγον⸃ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν.
english_snapshot: he certainly need not honor his father[a][b]. And you have nullified the word of God for the sake of your tradition.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the commandment of God' instead of 'the word of God.'

source_text: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἐνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια ⸀Μαγαδάν.
english_snapshot: And after dismissing the crowds[a], he got into the boat and came to the region of Magadan.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Magdala' instead of 'Magadan.'

source_text: Τοῦτο δὲ τὸ γένος οὐκ ἐκπορεύεται εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ καὶ νηστείᾳ.
english_snapshot: But[a] this kind does not come out except by prayer and fasting.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Syriac and Coptic translations, but is present in the Byzantine majority tradition, the Latin tradition, and most Syriac witnesses. It was likely added by later scribes to harmonize with Mark 9:29.

source_text: Ἦλθεν γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός.
english_snapshot: For the Son[a] of Man came to save the lost.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations, but is present in the 5th-century Codex Bezae, the Byzantine majority tradition, and the Latin Vulgate. It was likely added by later scribes to harmonize with Luke 19:10.

source_text: Ἐὰν δὲ ἁμαρτήσῃ ⸂εἰς σὲ⸃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου, ⸀ὕπαγε ἔλεγξον αὐτὸν μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου. ἐάν σου ἀκούσῃ, ἐκέρδησας τὸν ἀδελφόν σου·
english_snapshot: But if your brother sins against you[a], go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he listens to you[b][c], you have gained your brother.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit 'against you,' reading, 'If your brother sins, go and confront him between you and him alone.'

source_text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται ⸂καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσας μοιχᾶται⸃.
english_snapshot: But I tell you that whoever divorces his wife[a], except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery[b]; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit: 'and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.'

source_text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με ⸂ἐρωτᾷς περὶ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ; εἷς ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαθός⸃· εἰ δὲ θέλεις ⸂εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν⸃, ⸀τήρησον τὰς ἐντολάς.
english_snapshot: And he said to him[a], “Why do you ask me about what is good? One is good. But if you want to enter into life[b], keep the commandments.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts and the parallel accounts read, 'Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God.' Matthew's SBLGNT text instead reads, 'Why do you ask me about what is good? One is the good one.'

source_text: ⸂Καὶ ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τοῦτον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφ’ ὃν δ’ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν.⸃
english_snapshot: And the one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces[a]; but on whomever it falls[b], it will crush him.

signals.text: The verse is absent in some manuscripts of Matthew, though it is paralleled in Luke 20:18.

source_text: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι κατεσθίετε τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν, καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι· διὰ τοῦτο λήψεσθε περισσότερον κρίμα.
english_snapshot: Woe[a] to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows' houses, and as a pretext make long prayers; therefore you will receive greater condemnation.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations, but is preserved in the Byzantine majority tradition, the Old Latin, the Vulgate, and the Syriac. It was likely added by later scribes to harmonize with similar statements in Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47. Manuscripts that include it vary on whether it appears before or after verse 13.

source_text: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι τῶν οὐρανῶν ⸂οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός⸃, εἰ μὴ ὁ ⸀πατὴρ μόνος.
english_snapshot: But concerning that day and hour[a], no one knows—not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son—except the Father alone.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit 'nor the Son.' The main text follows the SBLGNT reading.

source_text: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἀνέκειτο μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα ⸀μαθητῶν
english_snapshot: When evening came[a], he reclined at the table with the twelve disciples.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read simply 'with the twelve' instead of 'with the twelve disciples.'

source_text: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά ⸀μου ⸀τῆς διαθήκης τὸ περὶ πολλῶν ἐκχυννόμενον εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·
english_snapshot: For this is my blood of the covenant[a][b], which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'my blood of the new covenant.'

source_text: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Καὶ ἔλαβον τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, τὴν τιμὴν τοῦ τετιμημένου ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ,
english_snapshot: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled[a], saying, ‘And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who had been valued[b], whom they valued from among the sons of Israel,’

signals.text: Matthew attributes this prophetic word to Jeremiah. The wording most closely parallels Zechariah 11:12–13, and interpreters variously explain this as a composite citation, a reference to a prophetic collection, or a textual problem in transmission.

source_text: εἶχον δὲ τότε δέσμιον ἐπίσημον λεγόμενον ⸀Ἰησοῦν Βαραββᾶν.
english_snapshot: At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read simply 'Barabbas,' omitting 'Jesus.'

source_text: συνηγμένων οὖν αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν, ⸂Ἰησοῦν τὸν⸃ Βαραββᾶν ἢ Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν;
english_snapshot: So when they had gathered together[a], Pilate said to them, “Which one do you want me to release to you: Jesus Barabbas[b], or Jesus who is called Messiah?”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read simply 'Barabbas' instead of 'Jesus Barabbas.'

source_text: ἐν αἷς ἦν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ ⸀Ἰωσὴφ μήτηρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου.
english_snapshot: among whom were Mary Magdalene[a], and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

signals.text: Some manuscripts/readings have 'Joses' instead of 'Joseph.'

source_text: κέλευσον οὖν ἀσφαλισθῆναι τὸν τάφον ἕως τῆς τρίτης ἡμέρας, μήποτε ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ κλέψωσιν αὐτὸν καὶ εἴπωσιν τῷ λαῷ· Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἐσχάτη πλάνη χείρων τῆς πρώτης.
english_snapshot: Therefore[a], order the tomb to be secured until the third day, lest his disciples come and steal him and say to the people[b], ‘He has been raised from the dead,’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.

signals.text: Some manuscripts add 'by night' after 'come': 'lest his disciples come by night and steal him away.' The shorter reading is followed here.
